destinations.name: Giza
destinations.summary: The last surviving wonder of the ancient world, rising from the desert.
destinations.story: The Great Pyramid of Khufu was built around 2560 BCE and was the tallest human-made structure in the world for thousands of years. It stands with the pyramids of Khafre and Menkaure on the Giza plateau, near the Great Sphinx, at the edge of modern Cairo.

stamp.alt: Stamp illustration of three pyramids and a camel with rider in warm desert light.

destinations.name: Cape Town
destinations.summary: A flat-topped mountain watching over the city and the Atlantic.
destinations.story: Table Mountain's level summit rises about 1,085 metres above Cape Town and is often draped in a cloud known as the tablecloth. Visitors reach the top on hiking trails or by rotating cable car, and the mountain lies within Table Mountain National Park.

stamp.alt: Stamp illustration of the flat-topped Table Mountain with a band of cloud above the city and blue sea.

destinations.name: Serengeti
destinations.summary: Endless savanna and the great wildebeest migration.
destinations.story: Serengeti National Park in northern Tanzania protects vast plains that are home to lions, elephants, giraffes and many other animals. Each year, large herds of wildebeest and zebra follow the rains in one of the world's great animal migrations.

stamp.alt: Stamp illustration of acacia trees, giraffes and distant herds on the golden savanna.

destinations.name: Marrakech
destinations.summary: A twelfth-century minaret guiding visitors through the medina.
destinations.story: The minaret of the Koutoubia Mosque, built in the 12th century, rises about 77 metres above the old city of Marrakech and serves as a landmark. Nearby, the square of Jemaa el-Fnaa fills each evening with food stalls, storytellers and musicians.

stamp.alt: Stamp illustration of the square, patterned Koutoubia minaret between palm trees in warm evening light.

destinations.name: Victoria Falls
destinations.summary: A mile-wide curtain of water on the Zambezi River.
destinations.story: Victoria Falls, known locally as Mosi-oa-Tunya or 'the smoke that thunders', lies on the border of Zambia and Zimbabwe. The Zambezi plunges more than a hundred metres into a narrow gorge, sending up spray that can be seen from far away. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

stamp.alt: Stamp illustration of a wide curtain of white water over a cliff with spray and a rainbow.
